svg.text: DIGITAL WIREFRAME — reference for hand sketch (not the milestone sketch itself)
B · Stand where you feel — exhibition · animatic
Who leads: audience (body position) inside an authored loop · floor projection + 2 walls
Where do you stand on AI?
Floor scale excited ↔ concerned, plus a 'none of these' zone of equal
size. Dots drift. One line on the wall invites you to step on.
Data: ai_sentiment answer scale, original order.
1,000 dots (1 dot ≈ 1 in 1,000 US adults) flow into piles on each
spot. The visitor sees how many stand where they stand.
348 of 1,000 Americans stand here with you
Neutral wording for every spot. 'None of these' gets the same
sentence and the same light — no spot is 'better'.
Wall text counts the people on your spot. Several visitors at once =
several rings. Works for groups and for the 'none of these' spot.
FLOOR — crowd splits into 4 age lanes
18–34 vs 65+: real gap · 18–34 vs 35–49: within margin → say 'about the same'
The crowd splits into 4 lanes by age. Concerned: 18–34 61, 35–49 66,
Data: ai_sentiment × age_18_34 / 35_49 / 50_64 / 65_plus. Only gaps above
the margin of error are called gaps.
people like me can shape it
it's coming whether we want it or not
Floor flips to the 2nd question. Visitor
moves again. Dots re-sort — not tracked from
The floor flips: 'can shape' ↔ 'coming anyway'. Visitors re-position.
The younger lane lights up larger on 'can shape'.
Data: ai_agency: can shape 17.4 %, inevitable 67.5 %, neither 14.0 %, no
Two walls, never one chart: a room next to a country
6 · A room next to a country
Close: US dots on one wall, today's room tally on the other.
Passers-by who never step on still see the loop 1 → 2 → 4 → 5.
Data: own visitor answers: never mixed into the dataset (project brief §05).
All numbers: US adults, 2026-09-10 to 2026-09-14, n = 1,083 · weighted % · pilot wave excluded · source exercises/W39_data/survey_all_waves_all_subgroups.csv · generated by make_wireframes.py
